core_obligations: Note that the composite K_0(Coh(Z)) -> K_0(D_{Z,perf}(O_X)) -> K_0(Coh(Z)) is the identity, so it suffices to prove surjectivity of the first arrow (proof lines 13012-13019).

For an object E of D_{Z,perf}(O_X), use regularity of X to know that its cohomology sheaves are coherent, supported on Z and nonzero only finitely often, and use the distinguished triangles of canonical truncation to write [E] = sum (-1)^i [H^i(E)[0]] in K_0(D_{Z,perf}(O_X)) (proof lines 13019-13030).

Reduce the remaining case of a coherent O_X-module set theoretically supported on Z: a finite filtration with quotients that are O_Z-modules exhibits its class in the image of the first arrow (proof lines 13030-13035).
proof_roadmap: One composite is the identity, so only surjectivity is needed (proof lines 13012-13019).
Decompose an arbitrary perfect complex into its shifted cohomology sheaves through canonical truncations (proof lines 13019-13030).
Handle a coherent module supported on Z by a finite filtration with O_Z-quotients (proof lines 13030-13035).
difficulty_reason: For a Noetherian regular scheme X and a closed subscheme Z, the lemma asserts that the two maps constructed in the preceding remarks are mutually inverse, giving K'_0(Z) = K_0(D_{Z,perf}(O_X)) (statement lines 13002-13009). The proof observes that one composite is the identity, so it remains to show that the map K_0(Coh(Z)) -> K_0(D_{Z,perf}(O_X)) is surjective (proof lines 13012-13019). The substance is the reduction of an arbitrary perfect complex supported on Z to its cohomology sheaves: regularity gives D_perf(O_X) = D^b_Coh(O_X), so the cohomology sheaves H^i(E) are coherent, may be regarded as objects of D_{Z,perf}(O_X), and are nonzero for only finitely many i, and the canonical truncation triangles then give [E] = sum (-1)^i [H^i(E)[0]] in the K-group (proof lines 13019-13030). It remains to see that the class of a coherent module set theoretically supported on Z lies in the image, which follows by taking a finite filtration with quotients that are O_Z-modules (proof lines 13030-13035). The use of the resolution property of a regular scheme together with the truncation decomposition is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
